findings.text: [Winogender](/evals/winogender) accuracy is higher on stereotypical examples than gotcha examples, and lowest on female gotcha examples; reported slice gaps improve with more shots.

source.quote:
We find that accuracy is higher on stereotypical examples than on gotcha examples, and that accuracy is
lowest on gotcha examples for female gender.

findings.text: Religion co-occurrence analysis associates Islam with charged stereotypes such as terrorist, violent, and radical.

source.quote:
see in Table 37 that Islam is associated with highly charged terms and stereotypes such as terrorist, violent
and radical, similar to other evaluations of decoder-only models revealing anti-Muslim bias (Abid et al., 2021).

findings.text: About 70% of top-10 co-occurring descriptors match between PaLM 62B and 540B across race, religion, and gender prompts.

source.quote:
On average, 70% of
the top-10 words are the same for the 62B and 540B models across race, religion and gender dimensions.

findings.text: Model continuation toxicity tracks prompt toxicity more closely than human continuations, suggesting like-to-like prompting effects.

source.quote:
Model
TPC is more consistent with the TPP than the human TPC, suggesting that the model is strongly influenced
by the prompt-style and is likely to respond like-to-like.

findings.text: Fairness analyses are English-only and narrowly scoped; the authors warn of biases beyond measured axes and recommend application-level assessment before deployment.

source.quote:
A major limitation of the fairness analyses presented in this section is that they are performed only on
English language data, while PaLM is trained on multilingual data and evaluated on multilingual language

findings.text: Training-set memorization rises with model scale and with how often an example was seen; examples seen more than 500 times exceed 40% memorization for the largest model.

source.quote:
examples seen more than 500 times have a memorization rate of
over 40%.

findings.text: The authors observed memorization of stories, news articles, and facts in addition to formulaic boilerplate.

source.quote:
However, we also observed memorization of stories, news articles, and
facts.

findings.text: PaLM should not be used for downstream applications without prior safety and fairness assessment; mitigation is recommended at the application level.

source.quote:

notes: Technical report (not a system card). Safety content is mainly Section 10 (Winogender, identity co-occurrence, RealToxicityPrompts), Section 7 memorization, Ethical Considerations, and BIG-bench BBQ Lite / HHH alignment rows. Figure 20–23 toxicity/Winogender charts lack readable numeric labels beyond the prose figures already extracted; religion toxicity distributions (Figure 22) are image-only. Capability suites (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, SuperGLUE, TyDiQA, translation, English NLP averages, most BIG-bench tasks) skipped per pilot safety-only rule. No external safety testers or formal risk-tier decisions. Datasheet notes training data collected 2019–2021 but no explicit model knowledge cutoff or product release date.
